name: Soft Actor-Critic for Discrete Action Spaces (SAC-Discrete)
key_paper: Christodoulou, P. (2019). Soft Actor-Critic for Discrete Action Spaces. arXiv:1910.07207. Derived from Haarnoja et al., SAC: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep RL with a Stochastic Actor, ICML 2018.
algorithm_description: SAC-Discrete extends the continuous Soft Actor-Critic algorithm to finite discrete action spaces. The Actor outputs a categorical probability distribution over all actions via a softmax head; the two Q-Critics (to reduce overestimation bias) receive only the state and return Q-values for every action simultaneously in a single forward pass, avoiding the need to enumerate transitions. The policy is trained to maximise a weighted combination of expected return and policy entropy H(pi), with the entropy coefficient alpha tuned automatically via a dual-gradient-descent objective targeting a minimum entropy threshold. The target entropy is typically set to -log(1/|A|) * 0.98. Off-policy replay buffer training makes it highly sample-efficient compared to on-policy methods.
action_space_handling: Fully discrete flat action space. The Actor outputs a softmax distribution over |A| actions; the Critics output |A| Q-values per state, making evaluation O(1) rather than O(|A|) queries. Actions are sampled from the categorical distribution during training and chosen greedily (or via temperature) at inference. The method does not natively handle structured or combinatorial action spaces without adaptation.
how_combinatorial_output_is_formed: In the vanilla formulation SAC-Discrete does not produce combinatorial outputs natively. To select k distinct numbers from {1..N} it must be adapted: the most straightforward extension is autoregressive masking, where the Actor is queried k times sequentially; after each selection the chosen number is masked to zero probability (via -inf logit) before the next sample. An alternative is to treat the entire k-subset as a single atomic action (|A| = C(N,k)), which is intractable for N=50, k=7. The autoregressive-masked variant is practical and retains entropy regularization at each step.
sequential_generation_strategy: When adapted for combinatorial output via autoregressive masking, numbers are generated one at a time conditioned on previously selected numbers (autoregressive). Inter-number correlations can be modeled if the Actor's input at step t includes the already-selected set (e.g., as a multi-hot mask appended to the state). In the unadapted flat form, generation is joint/flat (single pass, no correlation modeling).
gradient_estimator_type: No discrete gradient estimator is needed for the Actor because the expected Q-value is computed as a closed-form dot product between the softmax probabilities and the Q-vector: E_a[Q(s,a)] = pi(s)^T Q(s). This is a simple sum, fully differentiable through the softmax without REINFORCE or Gumbel-softmax. This is the key computational advantage of SAC-Discrete over policy-gradient methods.
combinatorial_constraint_enforcement: Autoregressive masking: after selecting number i at step t, the Actor's logit for i is set to -inf before softmax at step t+1, guaranteeing distinctness. This is applied at both training-time (when generating transitions) and inference-time. No rejection sampling loop is needed. The k constraint (select exactly k) is enforced by running exactly k autoregressive steps.
sample_efficiency_rating: Medium-high. SAC-Discrete is off-policy and uses an experience replay buffer, making it far more sample-efficient than on-policy methods (PPO, A2C). Entropy regularization prevents premature convergence and helps exploration on sparse data. However, the Q-function needs meaningful return signal to stabilize, and with fewer than 100 training episodes it may take many epochs before the Critics converge. Rated medium (not high) because the reward signal in the lottery domain is very sparse and near-random, limiting how much the Q-function can learn even with good replay efficiency.
regularization_built_in: Maximum entropy objective: the policy is penalized for low entropy at every update step, preventing mode collapse and encouraging exploration. Automatic entropy tuning (alpha dual update) adapts the regularization strength dynamically. Double-Q Critics reduce overestimation. Polyak-averaged target networks provide stable bootstrapping targets. No explicit dropout or weight decay in the base algorithm, but they can be added to network layers.
known_failure_modes_on_small_data: Q-function divergence: with very few transitions in the replay buffer, bootstrapped TD targets are noisy and can cause Q-value explosion, especially early in training. Entropy collapse: if alpha decays too fast, the policy can collapse to a near-deterministic mapping before the Q-function has learned anything useful. Reward sparsity amplification: in the lottery domain almost all plays score 0 hits; the Critic may converge to a near-zero Q-function for all actions, making the entropy bonus the only gradient signal (essentially random play). Overestimation bias: even with double-Q, small batches from a sparse-reward buffer can exhibit high variance in Q-targets.
data_regime_evidence: The original SAC-Discrete paper (Christodoulou 2019) was evaluated on Atari games with hundreds of thousands of environment steps -- not a small-data regime. Subsequent work applying SAC-Discrete to tabular or low-data domains is sparse in the literature. No published benchmark directly tests SAC-Discrete with fewer than 200 training episodes in a combinatorial-output setting. The algorithm's off-policy nature and replay buffer mean it can re-use all historical draws (e.g., 100 draws replayed many times), which partially compensates for small n, but this is a compensatory mechanism rather than empirical validation at n<200. minimum_training_samples_tested: [uncertain]. performance_degradation_curve: not published for n<200. comparison_baseline: [uncertain].
convergence_guarantees_small_n: No finite-sample convergence bounds exist for SAC-Discrete in the literature. The continuous SAC has asymptotic convergence analysis under tabular / linear function approximation assumptions, but these do not transfer to deep network critics on small datasets. Empirically, practitioners report that SAC-Discrete is more stable than DQN variants on sparse rewards due to entropy regularization, but this is anecdotal. Convergence in the lottery domain with n<200 draws is [uncertain] and likely very slow given reward sparsity.
reward_distribution_handling: SAC-Discrete can work with sparse, skewed rewards but requires careful design. The lottery reward distribution (~95% zero-hit, ~4% 1-2 hits, rare 3+ hits) means most replay buffer transitions carry zero reward. Distributional extensions (C51, QR-DQN style) are not built-in but can be grafted onto the Critic. The entropy bonus provides a non-zero gradient signal even when all rewards are zero, which is the primary mechanism keeping training alive in sparse-reward regimes. The minimum draws needed for stable Critic learning is approximately 500-1000 transitions in practice (achievable by replaying 100 draws many times). Semi-bandit (number-level) reward signal is not natively supported but can be incorporated by shaping the reward to count individual number hits.
credit_assignment_granularity: By default, SAC-Discrete assigns credit at the play level (set-level): the reward is +k for k number hits per play. For number-level credit assignment, the reward function must be shaped manually (e.g., reward = hits / k). The autoregressive extension enables partial credit: each number selection step can receive a sub-reward based on whether that number appeared in the draw, implementing semi-bandit feedback and dramatically improving credit assignment granularity on small datasets.
diversity_mechanism: The maximum entropy objective directly encourages the policy distribution to remain broad. High entropy => diverse plays across draws. The temperature parameter alpha controls the diversity-exploitation tradeoff and is tuned automatically. At prediction time, diversity across multiple plays is achieved by sampling multiple times from the stochastic policy. There is no explicit inter-play diversity reward by default; plays could still be similar if the policy distribution is multimodal with narrow peaks. An explicit diversity bonus (e.g., Hamming distance between generated plays) can be added to the reward.
offline_vs_online_rl_compatibility: SAC-Discrete is an off-policy algorithm and can be trained on a fixed historical replay buffer containing all past draws, making it compatible with the offline setting (one draw per week). The replay buffer is simply pre-populated with all historical draw observations. However, without new environment interaction the Q-function may exhibit distributional shift artifacts (overestimated Q-values for out-of-distribution actions), analogous to offline RL pathologies. Conservative regularization (CQL penalty) can be added to mitigate this. Overall it is more offline-compatible than on-policy methods (PPO/A2C) but less robust than purpose-built offline RL algorithms (CQL, IQL).
complexity: Medium. The base SAC-Discrete is straightforward to implement in PyTorch (~300-400 lines). Integrating with the existing SharedLotteryTransformer backbone and adapting for autoregressive combinatorial output adds complexity. Automatic alpha tuning and double-Q target networks are standard boilerplate.
key_dependencies: PyTorch only for core algorithm. Optional: torchrl (provides SAC-Discrete components and replay buffer utilities). No mandatory external RL library required.
estimated_lines_of_code: 350-500 lines: Actor head with autoregressive masking (~80 lines), double-Q Critic head (~60 lines), replay buffer (~80 lines), SAC-Discrete training loop with alpha auto-tuning (~150 lines), integration with existing SharedLotteryTransformer encoder (~50 lines), prediction wrapper (~40 lines).
transfer_learning_compatibility: High compatibility. The SharedLotteryTransformer encoder produces a state embedding that can be directly fed into the SAC-Discrete Actor and Critic heads without modification. The Actor and Critic are implemented as lightweight MLP heads attached to the frozen or fine-tuned encoder output. The lottery_id embedding already differentiates lotteries, so a single Actor/Critic pair can serve all three lotteries or separate heads can be used per lottery. Fine-tuning the encoder jointly with the Actor/Critic is also feasible.
specific_application_in_project: In Phase 2, SAC-Discrete replaces the current temperature-softmax sampling in predict.py. The SharedLotteryTransformer encoder output (state) feeds into two lightweight MLP Q-Critics and one Actor with autoregressive masking. The replay buffer is pre-loaded with all historical draws (draws.csv, draws_649.csv, draws_dailygrand.csv) encoded as (state, action, reward, next_state) tuples where action = the play that was generated, reward = number of hits against the actual draw. The Actor generates plays by selecting 7 numbers (LottoMax) autoregressively with masking. After each new draw is logged via main_swarm.py log, the SAC-Discrete loop runs N update steps on the expanded buffer. Thompson sampling bandit weights in bandit.py can be updated using the per-play hit scores as before. This addresses the current limitation that predict.py has no feedback loop connecting historical hit scores back to play generation.
replaces_or_extends: Replaces temperature-softmax sampling in src/predict.py. Extends the system by adding a Critic (Q-function) component alongside the existing Actor (transformer encoder + softmax head). The encoder backbone is reused, not replaced.
existing_open_source_implementations: 1. Original author implementation: github.com/p-christ/Deep-Reinforcement-Learning-Algorithms-with-PyTorch (SAC_Discrete agent). 2. torchrl library (PyTorch, Meta): includes SACLoss and discrete policy components. 3. stable-baselines3 does NOT include SAC-Discrete natively (only continuous SAC). 4. CleanRL: cleanrl/sac_atari.py provides a clean single-file implementation for Atari discrete environments. 5. Ray RLlib: supports SAC with discrete action spaces via config.
benchmark_results: Christodoulou (2019): SAC-Discrete matches or exceeds DQN, DDQN, and Dueling DQN on 6 Atari games (Pong, Breakout, Space Invaders, etc.) with substantially fewer environment steps, demonstrating superior sample efficiency. Entropy regularization prevents the policy collapse observed in DQN variants on sparse-reward Atari levels. No published results on combinatorial discrete action spaces or lottery-style prediction tasks.
notable_use_cases: 1. Discrete robot control (joint angle discretized). 2. Game playing with discrete moves (Atari, board games). 3. Recommendation systems with discrete item selection (structurally similar to lottery: select k items from N, sparse implicit reward). 4. Discrete molecular design (select atoms/bonds sequentially -- analogous to selecting numbers autoregressively). 5. Network routing with discrete path selection. None published specifically for lottery number prediction.
